topic: A CRA balance-owing notice: three usual causes to check, the 90-day windows and daily interest (federal rules; Manitoba rate used only in the example)

example.note: example: Manitoba resident with taxable income about $80,000 before the missed slip (federal 20.5% band $58,523–$117,045, Manitoba 12.75% band $47,000–$100,000 for 2026); nothing withheld on interest income; credits unchanged; instalment bars are illustrative net tax owing amounts (example)

sources.reassess: ITA 152(3.1)(b), 152(4): CRA may reassess an individual within the normal reassessment period, 3 years after the original notice of assessment
sources.interest: ITA 161(1): interest at the prescribed rate on tax unpaid after the balance-due day; 248(1) balance-due day of an individual = April 30 of the following year; 248(11): compounded daily
sources.instalments: ITA 156.1(1): instalments required when net tax owing exceeds the instalment threshold ($3,000; $1,800 in Quebec) for the year and for either of the two preceding years; 161(2): instalment interest
sources.collection: ITA 225.1(1), (1.1)(c): no legal collection actions until 90 days after the day the notice of assessment was sent; 225.1(2): after an objection, none until 90 days after CRA confirms or varies
sources.objection: ITA 165(1)(a): an individual may object by the later of one year after the filing-due date and 90 days after the notice was sent
sources.rates: ITA 117(2) (federal 2026) and Manitoba Budget 2025 p.140 / CRA T4127 2026 (Manitoba brackets), as verified for H4
